sections.h2: Where is the Harnett County Register of Deeds and what does it record?
sections.html:
Look for Suite 200 at 305 W. Cornelius Harnett Blvd, Lillington, NC 27546. Land documents of every kind end up here: deeds, mortgages, plats, powers of attorney and UCC filings. Voters choose the person who runs the office every two years, as G.S. 161-1 provides.

All of it is open to the public except military discharges. Harnett County was formed from Cumberland County in 1855, and the books go back to that year, although fires in 1892 and 1894 destroyed many early records.

By statute, the staff may not run title searches. A seller or buyer who wants the chain of title needs an attorney or a title company. Because the index runs by name, a person who only has a street address should look up the owner in the county GIS viewer first.

sections.h2: What are the Harnett County recording fees?
sections.html:
The posted schedule is dated July 1, 2026 and follows G.S. 161-10. An ordinary deed starts at $26.00 and a mortgage or deed of trust at $64.00, with $4.00 charged for each page beyond the included count.

Harnett County recording charges, schedule dated July 1, 2026
ItemCharge
Deed or other instrument, pages 1 to 15$26.00
Added pages, either type$4.00 each
Deed of trust or mortgage, pages 1 to 35$64.00
Satisfaction or cancellationNone
Plat, per page$21.00
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each after
Extra subsequent-instrument index reference$25.00

Source: Harnett County Register of Deeds uniform fee schedule. Because releasing a loan costs nothing to record, a payoff at closing adds no recording charge on that side.

sections.h2: What deed tax applies to a Harnett County sale?
sections.html:
The county prints the rate as $2.00 per $1,000, which is the same as $1.00 for each $500 of price or fraction of $500. Its history table shows that rate in force since August 1, 1991, after a 50-cent rate that began in 1968.

The seller settles it ahead of recording. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the money is split between the county general fund and the state, which receives its half monthly after a small county allowance.

Have the closing attorney show this tax as a separate seller line on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: When does a deed count as recorded in Harnett County?
sections.html:
A deed counts when the staff has keyed it in. Walk-ins face no set cutoff, yet anything that cannot be keyed by 5:00 p.m. waits for the following business day, and electronic submissions stop at 4:45 p.m.

The clock matters because priority runs in order of registration. G.S. 47-18 gives a conveyance, option, lease beyond three years or first-refusal right no force against lien creditors or paying buyers until the instrument is registered in the home county of the land.

  • E-recording is offered for every document type, maps and plats included.
  • Maps are accepted only at 24x36 or 18x24 inches.
  • Copy requests by mail go to the Suite 200 address, and certified copies of land records are arranged by contacting the office.

sections.h2: What should a Harnett seller verify ahead of signing?
sections.html:
Check that the deed names the record owner exactly. The register cannot add or remove names from an existing deed, so any correction means drafting a fresh one, and the office advises using an attorney unless the owner is comfortable with legal drafting.

  • Search the grantor index under the owner's name for open deeds of trust, then ask each lender for a payoff.
  • If another person will sign, look for a recorded power of attorney. Healthcare powers are not recorded here.
  • For an inherited house, make sure the estate papers are with the clerk of court, where divorce and estate files are kept.
  • Get the unpaid-tax balance from the Tax Department in Suite 101 of the same address.

Separation agreements appear at this office only if someone recorded them. A seller who is separating should find out whether one exists and whether it mentions the house.

sections.h2: Can I request copies from the Harnett County register?
sections.html:
Visit the office, mail a request to the Suite 200 address, or use the county's online record search. Plain copies are $0.25 each on the posted schedule.

Searches work best with the exact spelling used on the instrument, so try the seller's name, a spouse's name and any former trust or company name. For older chains, remember the 1892 and 1894 fires, which means a closing attorney may have to start from later instruments.

The office also records assumed business names, at $26.00 on paper or $41.00 filed online, along with fixture filings under the UCC. Neither touches a house sale unless the property secures a business loan.

sections.h2: How do I find a plat or map in Harnett County?
sections.html:
Use the online record search with a map book and page, entered under the Advanced tab. Maps stored in a plat cabinet use a different pattern: type PC# and the cabinet letter in the book field, and put the slide number with its letter in the page field, with no space or dash between them.

For example, Plat Cabinet C, Slide 123-B is entered as PC#C in the book field and 123B in the page field. The office also keeps an index to plats for browsing by hand.

A lot-line question is common when an older house is listed. If the survey on file looks out of date, the seller may want a fresh one before the buyer's attorney asks. A plat recorded here costs $21.00 per page.

sections.h2: Who records a deed after a Harnett County tax foreclosure sale?
sections.html:
The winning bidder does. After the court confirms a Harnett County tax foreclosure sale, the bidder receives a commissioner's deed, and the county's foreclosure page makes recording it with the register the bidder's own job, to be done promptly.

That page also says properties sell as is, with no warranty from the county or the commissioner, and that sales are not conditioned on financing or marketable title. An owner facing that process may redeem before confirmation, or sell to someone who can close first, and that deed is recorded here as usual.

sections.h2: Which Census numbers frame a Harnett County sale?
sections.html:
Census Bureau figures describe the people a Harnett County seller is marketing to. These are the ones most tied to housing.

  • 49,845 households for 2020-2024, averaging 2.73 persons.
  • Age and service: 14.7% of the population is 65 or older, and the county counts 11,660 veterans.
  • Rent and carrying costs: gross rent has a median of $1,112, and mortgaged owners carry a median of $1,594 monthly.
  • Stability: 86.8% of people aged one and over had not moved in the prior year.
  • Land area is 594.93 square miles, with 224.5 people per square mile counted in 2020 (Census QuickFacts).

Workers average 32.8 minutes of travel to work, a figure buyers weigh against the price of a house.

faqs.q: Price of recording a Harnett deed?
faqs.a: Budget $26.00 for a deed of up to 15 pages, with $4.00 added per extra page. A deed of trust runs $64.00 up to 35 pages. Those are the numbers on the schedule dated July 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Who covers the Harnett County deed excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller, as the transferor, covers it, and it goes to the register ahead of recording. The rate is $1.00 for every $500 of consideration or value.

faqs.q: Will the register of deeds check my title for me?
faqs.a: No. State law keeps the staff from doing title searches. An attorney, a title company or the owner can search the name-indexed records, and the GIS viewer helps connect a name to an address.

faqs.q: How late in the day can a Harnett County deed be recorded?
faqs.a: In person, it must be keyed before 5:00 p.m., and that turns on how long the document takes to enter. E-recordings must arrive by 4:45 p.m. Later items are recorded on the next business day.

faqs.q: Does it cost anything to record a mortgage satisfaction in Harnett County?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule lists satisfactions and cancellations of deeds of trust at no charge, and the lender normally files the release once the loan is paid off.
